learningObjectives: Explain how Vision AI identifies and steers controls, and which technologies it uses.
Distinguish Vision AI from conventional property-based scanning and from image-based controls.
Describe User Identified Controls (UIDCs) and the role of anchors within Vision AI.
Judge when Vision AI is the appropriate scanning approach.

elements.text: This lesson is labeled optional in the local AE1 outline. The current Academy exam blueprint was not accessible for verification, so do not infer that the topic can never appear in an exam. Check the current official course requirements. This guide explains the documented on-prem Vision AI mechanisms.

elements.term: Seeing the UI the way a person does
elements.description: Conventional scanning reads an application's technical structure — element ids, class names, the control tree. Vision AI instead analyses the application's visual components, using two neural networks: one for finding controls and one for optical character recognition (OCR). It identifies what is on screen much as a human tester would: this looks like a text field, that is a button labelled 'Submit'.

elements.term: Recognising control types, not just pixels
elements.description: The crucial detail is that Vision AI detects control types and adjusts its steering mechanism to the classification it has made. Having decided a region is a dropdown, it steers it as a dropdown. This is what separates it from raw appearance matching.

elements.title: Standard modules → Engines → Vision AI
items: Run VisionScript — executes a VisionScript, Tosca's scripting layer for Vision AI driven steering.
Vision AI Self Healing — the self-healing counterpart for visually recognised controls.

elements.text: Vision AI recovery requires administrator-enabled cloud image-analysis history, a Recovery Scenario with RetryLevel=TestStepValue, the Vision AI Self Healing Module, OnDialogFailure=Recover and TestStepValueRetries=1. Run from an ExecutionList. Recovery is attempted for missing controls; it does not guarantee that the intended target or later assertions will succeed.

bulletPoints: Two neural networks: control detection + OCR.
Identification is by visual components in the UI, not by technical attributes.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Vision AI vs the two methods you already know

elements.description: Vision AI uses visual recognition rather than relying on the target’s DOM identifiers. Changes to technical attributes may therefore leave a visual locator usable, but labels, layout, detection quality and steering support still require validation.

Image identifiers match a captured appearance. Vision AI detects control types and uses type-specific steering. Classification can require adjustment; neither method guarantees reliable execution after arbitrary visual changes.

elements.text: Evaluate Vision AI against the actual interface and supported steering behavior. The introduction documents table-steering limitations and suggests VisionScript for some cases. Marketing descriptions of stable or platform-agnostic automation are not a guarantee that every UI is supported.

bulletPoints: Property-based: reads structure. Image-based: matches pixels. Vision AI: recognises control types visually.
Vision AI ≠ a better screenshot matcher — it classifies what it sees and steers accordingly.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: When automatic recognition is not enough

elements.description: When detection is unsuitable, XScan can adjust the ControlType among detected choices, refine labels or create a User Identified Control (UIDC). In Advanced View, define the target region, control type and application category, select anchor controls, save and rescan. UIDC definitions are shared within the company.

UIDCs use reference controls inside or outside the target region. A single anchor preserves a fixed relative size/position and may fail when sizes vary. Prefer unique text labels and multiple appropriate anchors for variable dimensions; use UidcCategory for the defined application group.

elements.text: PDF, XScan and Vision AI anchors share a reference idea but have distinct configuration and behavior. PDF-specific rules are not a substitute for UIDC anchor selection.

bulletPoints: UIDC = a control you define manually when the AI's own classification is insufficient.
Anchor points guide the AI to the right target.

elements.title: Vision AI fits when
items: Application controls lack reliable technical identifiers.
UI layouts change frequently but the visual appearance stays consistent.
You can configure and validate recovery for missing visually recognized controls, with the required cloud-history policy.
Standard property-based identification has proved insufficient.

elements.text: These are independent selection considerations, not a universal vendor ranking. Compare identification reliability, supported controls, setup and cloud data requirements. A working structural locator does not automatically justify migration.
📄 The Vision AI Theory section is optional course material. Official Tricentis Academy content is not redistributed here — explore it inside the official course if you want the hands-on walkthrough.

bulletPoints: Candidate fit: unreliable technical identifiers or visually accessible interfaces; validate classification, steering and recovery.

examPitfalls.title: Treating an old optional label as an exam guarantee
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Skipping a topic because this local outline labels it optional.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the current official Academy blueprint. The local optional label is not verification that future or current exams exclude all Vision AI questions.

examPitfalls.title: Equating Vision AI with image-based controls
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Vision AI is simply a more advanced screenshot matcher.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Image-based identification matches appearance with no understanding of the control. Vision AI recognises individual control types and adjusts its steering to that classification — a different mechanism, not a refinement of the same one.

examPitfalls.title: Replacing working property-based scans with Vision AI
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Migrating stable, well-identified Modules to Vision AI on the assumption that newer is better.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Compare the actual identification and steering requirements before changing a working Module. Visual recognition may suit unreliable technical identifiers, but it brings detection, setup and data-policy considerations.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting perfect automatic classification
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Vision AI will correctly identify every control with no manual intervention.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When detection is unsuitable, XScan can adjust the ControlType among detected choices, refine labels or create a User Identified Control (UIDC). In Advanced View, define the target region, control type and application category, select anchor controls, save and rescan. UIDC definitions are shared within the company.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which two technologies does Vision AI use to identify UI elements?

options.text: The DOM parser and the UI Automation framework.
Two neural networks — one for finding controls and one for optical character recognition (OCR).
The Appium server and the Mobile Agent.

practiceQuiz.hint: One network locates things; the other reads text.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Vision AI employs two neural networks: one for finding controls and one for OCR. Together they let it identify elements by their visual components rather than by technical attributes.

optionExplanations.A: DOM and UI Automation are structural mechanisms; the documented visual detection/OCR parameters are different.
optionExplanations.B: Control detection and OCR provide the documented visual identification functions, configurable through ScanControlNetwork and ScanOcrNetwork.
optionExplanations.C: Checksums do not provide the documented type detection and OCR behavior.
optionExplanations.D: Appium and TMA manage mobile automation, not the described Vision AI recognition functions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the essential difference between Vision AI and image-based controls?

options.text: There is none — both match screenshots.
Vision AI recognises individual control types and adjusts its steering accordingly, rather than performing simple pixel matching or screenshot comparison.
Image-based controls use neural networks; Vision AI does not.
Vision AI only works on mobile applications.

practiceQuiz.hint: Compare type-aware visual steering with matching a captured appearance.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Vision AI detects control types and varies steering by type. This differs from matching a captured appearance; accurate classification and execution still need validation.

optionExplanations.A: Type-dependent steering differentiates Vision AI from matching a captured appearance.
optionExplanations.B: Vision AI detects types and uses type-dependent steering; unsuitable classification may need manual adjustment.
optionExplanations.C: This reverses the documented use of neural networks for Vision AI detection and OCR.
optionExplanations.D: Vision AI is not documented as a mobile-only mechanism; it is integrated with on-prem XScan for applications.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Vision AI fails to classify a particular control correctly. What can you do?

options.text: Nothing — Vision AI classifications cannot be overridden.
Configure the control manually or create a User Identified Control (UIDC), using anchor points to guide the AI to the target.
Switch the whole Module to the Mobile Engine.
Retake the screenshot at a higher resolution.

practiceQuiz.hint: There is a named mechanism for controls you define yourself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: XScan supports control-type and label adjustments and UIDCs using reference controls. Anchor quality, sizing and the application category affect recognition; creating a UIDC does not guarantee a correct target.

optionExplanations.A: XScan permits classification/label adjustment and UIDCs; recognition is not immutable.
optionExplanations.B: These are documented remediation mechanisms. Choose appropriate anchors and validate the resulting recognition.
optionExplanations.C: The Mobile Engine is not a universal remedy for a visually misclassified application control.
optionExplanations.D: A different screenshot resolution does not replace the documented classification or UIDC configuration workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which situation is the strongest case for using Vision AI?

options.text: A stable application whose controls all have reliable, unchanging ids.
An application whose markup changes frequently while its visual appearance stays consistent.
Reading values from an Excel workbook.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about when structural identification stops being dependable.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Among these choices, unstable technical markup with stable appearance is the clearest candidate for visual identification. Compare it with actual detection/steering support and validate the result; PDF comparison and Excel workbook operations have dedicated Modules.

optionExplanations.A: Stable identifiers alone do not establish a need to replace a working structural locator.
optionExplanations.B: Visual identification can reduce dependence on changing markup when the appearance remains suitable; reliability still needs testing.
optionExplanations.C: PDF file comparison is a dedicated PDF operation, not this control-identification use case.
optionExplanations.D: Workbook data access is an Excel operation, not this visual UI-identification use case.

Unreliable technical identifiers or visually accessible interfaces; validate supported controls, setup and data policy.
